slides.teacher_cue: What sound? Hold mirror — tongue curls back, no contact.
slides.expected_response: Students produce /r/ with tongue curled back, no contact with roof of mouth.
slides.correction_move: Model /r/ with mirror — tongue curves back, does not touch. Students repeat three times.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /l/ substitution or Korean flap /ɾ/. Mirror work is mandatory on this sound.

slides.teacher_cue: What sound?
slides.expected_response: Students produce /æ/ quickly and cleanly.
slides.correction_move: Model /æ/, students repeat three times, then recheck.
slides.observation_note: Watch for vowel quality — /æ/ is a front open-mid vowel. Korean speakers may produce a more centralised or raised variant.

slides.teacher_cue: What sound?
slides.expected_response: Students produce /ɪ/ quickly and cleanly.
slides.correction_move: Model /ɪ/, students repeat three times, then recheck.
slides.observation_note: Watch for vowel quality — /ɪ/ is a lax high front vowel. Korean speakers may substitute the tense /iː/.

slides.teacher_cue: Two sounds — say each. /s/ — air hisses out. /t/ — tongue tip taps ridge, quick stop.
slides.expected_response: Students produce /s/ and /t/ cleanly and distinctly.
slides.correction_move: Model each sound separately, then together. Students repeat chorally.
slides.observation_note: Watch for voicing on /s/ (should be voiceless) and aspiration on /t/ at word onset.

slides.teacher_cue: Play rat once. Replay only if needed before checking.
slides.expected_response: Students write rat accurately.
slides.correction_move: Replay rat once, segment orally, then recheck.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students encode the /r/ onset correctly — r not l.

slides.teacher_cue: Play rip once. Replay only if needed before checking.
slides.expected_response: Students write rip accurately.
slides.correction_move: Replay rip once, segment orally, then recheck.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students encode the /r/ onset correctly — r not l.

slides.teacher_cue: Play rack once. Replay only if needed before checking.
slides.expected_response: Students write rack accurately — note ck digraph.
slides.correction_move: Replay rack once, segment orally r-a-ck, then recheck.
slides.observation_note: Watch for r at onset and for correct spelling of ck at coda.

slides.teacher_cue: In Korean, /r/ and /l/ are one sound — the flap /ɾ/. In English they are two different phonemes that change word meaning. rip and lip are DIFFERENT words. Listen carefully — your ear must learn this difference. Hold a mirror: /r/ — tongue curls back, no contact with roof. /l/ — tongue tip touches the ridge behind front teeth. Mirror work mandatory.
slides.expected_response: Students understand that /r/ and /l/ are separate English phonemes and attempt both articulations with mirror.
slides.correction_move: Model each position with mirror — curl back for /r/, touch ridge for /l/. Students alternate slowly.
slides.observation_note: Watch for conflation of /r/ and /l/. This is a foundational awareness moment — note which students need the most articulatory support.

content_payload.correction_routine: rip starts with /r/ — tongue curls back. lip starts with /l/ — tongue touches ridge.

slides.teacher_cue: Play both words. Ask: Which word starts with /r/? Students point or say A or B.
slides.expected_response: Students identify A (rip) as the /r/-onset word.
slides.correction_move: Play each word again. Contrast the onset positions in mirror. Students repeat rip three times.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students can auditorily discriminate /r/ from /l/ at word onset. Note any who choose B consistently.

slides.teacher_cue: Play both words. Ask: Which word starts with /r/? Students point or say A or B.
slides.expected_response: Students identify A (rap) as the /r/-onset word.
slides.correction_move: Play each word again. Model /r/ vs /l/ onset articulation and have students repeat rap three times.
slides.observation_note: Watch for consistent /r/ vs /l/ discrimination. Two minimal pairs in a row builds auditory contrast.

slides.teacher_cue: Say rat — a small rodent. Tongue curls back for /r/ at onset — no contact with roof. Reveal print and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say rat with clean /r/ onset and connect meaning before blending.
slides.correction_move: Model /r/ with mirror, then model rat in full. Students repeat three times.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /l/ substitution at onset — 'lat' for 'rat'.

slides.teacher_cue: Say ran — past tense of run. Tongue curls back for /r/ at onset — no contact with roof. Reveal print and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say ran with clean /r/ onset and connect meaning before blending.
slides.correction_move: Model /r/ with mirror, then model ran in full. Students repeat three times.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /l/ substitution at onset — 'lan' for 'ran'.

slides.teacher_cue: Say rip — to tear. Tongue curls back for /r/ at onset — no contact with roof. Reveal print and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say rip with clean /r/ onset and connect meaning before blending.
slides.correction_move: Model /r/ with mirror, then model rip in full. Students repeat three times.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /l/ substitution at onset — 'lip' for 'rip'. Note: lip is a real word, so errors are semantically significant.

slides.teacher_cue: Say rick — a stack of hay. Tongue curls back for /r/ at onset — no contact with roof. Reveal print and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say rick with clean /r/ onset and connect meaning before blending.
slides.correction_move: Model /r/ with mirror, then model rick in full. Students repeat three times.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /l/ substitution at onset — 'lick' for 'rick'.

slides.teacher_cue: Say rap — to knock sharply. Tongue curls back for /r/ at onset — no contact with roof. Reveal print and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say rap with clean /r/ onset and connect meaning before blending.
slides.correction_move: Model /r/ with mirror, then model rap in full. Students repeat three times.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /l/ substitution at onset — 'lap' for 'rap'. Note: lap is a real word, so errors are semantically significant.

slides.teacher_cue: Say the sounds and build rat left to right.
